Executive Order 2008-6 declares a state of emergency for Allegan County after 'a series of severe storms moved through central and southern lower Michigan between June 6, 2008 and June 8, 2008'. The Governor's press release of June 13, 2008 says she 'today declared a state of emergency in Allegan, Eaton, and Mason counties and the cities of Lansing and Saginaw' (https://www.michigan.gov/formergovernors/recent/granholm/press-releases/2008/06/13/granholm-declares-state-of-emergency-in-lansing-saginaw-counties-of-allegan-eaton-mason).

Michigan Public, May 7, 2013: 'Governor Rick Snyder has declared a state of disaster across much of Michigan due to storm- and flood-related damage', covering Grand Rapids, Ionia and 19 counties. The Governor's June 21, 2013 release dates the flooding April 16 to May 14.

Governor's press release, August 13, 2014: Snyder 'today issued the following statement upon authorizing a state declaration of disaster for Wayne, Oakland and Macomb counties' after that week's flooding.

Governor's press release, June 23, 2017: 'Brian Calley today declared a state of disaster for Isabella and Midland counties after severe weather and intense rain', as Lieutenant Governor acting for Governor Snyder.

UPI, June 18, 2018: Gov. Snyder declared a disaster on Monday (June 18): 'The declaration was made for Houghton and Menominee counties after severe weather and heavy rainfall struck the area.' The Governor's June 21, 2018 release amends it to add Gogebic County.
